summary: Season/career database object factory. Validates a type id against the cache bounds, returns a cached object pointer when already built or for out-of-range ids, and for ids 1-45 allocates a per-type buffer, runs the matching constructor, installs the per-type vtable, caches the result in this[(id-1)+1607] and returns it. On allocation failure the cache slot is set to 0 and 0 is returned. Id 436 is handled specially with a 772-byte bulk-init object.

operations.description: Validate the id against the cache: a2-1 must be in [0, 507] and the cache slot this[(a2-1)+1607] must be empty; otherwise return 0 or the already-cached pointer.
Ids above 436 return the cached pointer without building a new object (only 436 has special handling).
Id 436: allocate 772 bytes and, on success, run the bulk-init-and-vtable constructor, cache the result and return it; on allocation failure store 0 in the cache slot and return that 0.

Id 1 (track database): allocate 236 bytes, run the byte-parameter constructor, set the string-buffer state (field 57 empty, field 58 length -1), install vtable off_5A7638, copy the track-db filename literal into the string buffer, then cache and return.
Id 2: allocate 380 bytes and run the FunctionCallWrapper_85b0 constructor, then cache and return.
Id 3: allocate 1108 bytes, run the zeroed-fields constructor, zero the four trailing fields (indices 273-276), install vtable off_5A6F48, cache and return.
Ids 5 and 6: allocate 848 bytes and run the ObjectConstructorWithVTable constructor, cache and return.
Ids 7 to 10 (UI components): allocate 232 bytes, run the UI-component init, install the per-type vtable (off_5A7588, off_5A74D8, off_5A7428, off_5A7378), cache and return.
Ids 11-15, 19, 25 and 26: allocate 384 bytes, run the large constructor, install vtable off_5A7218, cache and return.
Ids 16 and 22: allocate 412 bytes, run the large constructor, run a post-construction computation on the field at index 96, install vtable off_5A7168, cache and return.
Ids 17 and 24: allocate 396 bytes and run the specialized constructor that receives the type id, then cache and return.
Id 18: allocate 384 bytes, run the large constructor, install vtable off_5A70B8, cache and return.
Id 20: allocate 388 bytes, run the large constructor, zero the field at index 96, install vtable off_5A72C8, cache and return.
Ids 21 and 23: allocate 400 bytes and run the ShortComputation_66f0 constructor with the type id, cache and return.
Id 27: allocate 380 bytes and run the vtable-and-sub-init constructor, cache and return.
Id 28: allocate 524 bytes and run the fields-plus-vtable constructor, cache and return.
Ids 30, 32 and 33: allocate 384 bytes and run the ShortComputation_b580 constructor with flag 0; id 31 runs the same constructor with flag 1; cache and return.
Id 34: allocate 384 bytes and run the specialized 0x004750F0 constructor, cache and return.
Ids 35 and 36: allocate 372 bytes, run the base init, install vtable off_5A7008, cache and return.
Id 37: allocate 288 bytes and run the specialized 0x0047A9E0 constructor, cache and return.
Id 38: allocate 376 bytes and run the init-plus-vtable constructor, cache and return.
Ids 39 to 42: allocate 376 bytes, run the base init, install vtable off_5A6E98, set the flag field at index 93 to 1, cache and return; on allocation failure store 0 in the cache and return 0.
Id 43: allocate 376 bytes and run the ShortComputation_e7d0 constructor, then cache the result.
Id 44: allocate 376 bytes and run the vtable-state init constructor, then cache the result.
Id 45: allocate 228 bytes and run the byte-parameter constructor with both parameters zero, then cache the result.
Default (unhandled ids) and post-switch cases return the cached slot value; the dispatch is driven by the switch jump table pointer.
